01 / Shell · Launch film · 2023

Let material and silhouette
carry the image.

In the original

The launch film presents a sculptural, functional object. A continuous wooden sheet forms the top and bends into its legs.

For Odu

Warm wood. Controlled surroundings. A complete, readable form. Let the tabletop and panel legs make the composition.

Team test

Art director: define the hero composition and lighting reference: warm side light, readable edges and a complete silhouette.

CGI lead: match the approved look; check wood response, exposure and grounded shadows.

Material and silhouette are our reading of the imagery. The creators do not publish a complete production breakdown. Borrow the restraint; preserve Odu’s own geometry.

Open the launch film ↗Independent creator collaboration.

02 / LOEHR × Spot Studio · Three CGI films · 2022

Give the object
a distinctive world.

In the original

Spot Studio created distinct surreal worlds to emphasise each product’s design and craftsmanship, testing dunes, rocks and changes of scale.

For Odu

Build a restrained architectural world from the table’s proportions: broad planes, low horizontals and carefully sized negative space.

Team test

Art director: sketch two spaces from Odu’s proportions; specify how light separates the table from its surroundings.

CGI lead: block out both at real scale and translate the chosen spatial and lighting brief into the scene.

Architecture is our proposed Odu adaptation. LOEHR’s source describes surreal landscapes. Use the relationship between object and world; choose Odu’s own setting.

03 / Danthree Studio · Schneeweiss Interior · 4K folding table

Reveal information
in stages.

In the original

Edge light introduces the table. A warmer studio reveals options and details; folding, stacking and interiors then explain how it works.

For Odu

Edge → grain → legs → full table. Each view adds one piece of understanding before the complete reveal.

Team test

Art director: board four reveals; specify the framing and what the light reveals in each view.

CGI lead: implement that camera and lighting plan using the same accurate model and material throughout.

The Odu sequence is our proposal. Folding mechanisms, accessories and other 4K features do not transfer to Odu without product evidence.

04 / Vitra Classics · Graphic Thought Facility · 2021

Make every crop
a deliberate composition.

In the original

Tight, recognisable chair details create distinct colour palettes and suggest the different people and worlds the chair can belong to.

For Odu

Build detail ads around an edge, grain or support. Treat the crop, colour balance and empty space as a complete image.

Team test

Art director: define three crops, their colour balance and lighting references beside the complete-table image.

CGI lead: build those approved views for the final formats; check the surface holds up close.

This reference uses photography. The Eames chair is already recognisable from a detail; Odu needs an establishing image so the audience knows what the crops belong to.

05 / Transparent House · Studio TK furniture · 2022

Maintain
material credibility.

In the original

Photorealistic CGI reproduces furniture with attention to its materials, details and surrounding environment.

For Odu

Keep grain direction, finish, scale and contact shadows consistent. The table should feel like the same real object in every view.

Team test

Art director: specify lighting and surroundings that let the wood read honestly, supported by visual references.

CGI lead: match that brief and check both views against product photos, dimensions and confirmed materials.

These checks are our practical application, not a published Studio TK workflow. Confirm Odu’s wood species, finish and construction before making production claims.

Synthesis / A direction to test

One world. Four reveals.

A warm, quiet architectural setting. The table stays grounded as light and framing reveal its material, structure and complete form.

Illustrative crops of one Majeurs product photo. These explain the proposed sequence; they are not final campaign frames.

First creative test

One hero + two detail images.

Start with the complete table, one material crop and one support crop. Review the world and visual language together before developing motion.

How we judge it

Is Odu readable? Does the setting relate to its proportions? Does each crop add something? Do wood, scale and shadows agree across all three?

Lock product geometry and material references first. Film duration, final formats and deliverables remain open.

Team handoff · lighting direction and execution

Creative directorSet the audience takeaway and approve the mood, look and sequence.

Art directorDefine the world, compositions and lighting brief: source, warmth, contrast, shadows and what each shot reveals.

CGI leadTranslate the approved brief into the scene; coordinate lighting execution, validate geometry and materials, and flag constraints.

The CGI lead may also light the scene in a small team. That is execution of the agreed look; lighting direction is developed with the art director and approved by the creative director.
